relevance.rationale: A distinct paper from biane1998 (Adv. Math. 138, 'Representations of symmetric groups and free probability'), which IS in references.ts and IS cited at prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton, rem:non-commutative-probability-dictionary and cfs-comparison-summary. This 2000 paper is the follow-up that converts biane1998's asymptotic character theory into a *concentration criterion*: any normalized positive-definite function on S_q satisfying an explicit magnitude bound plus approximate multiplicativity on disjoint supports has its induced measure on Young diagrams concentrated near a single diagram. prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton clause (3) — 'for q != 1 the measures mu_n^{(q)} converge weakly' — is exactly this kind of statement, and is flagged conjectural. Biane 2000 supplies the q=1 template, i.e. the precise hypotheses a q-deformed argument would have to verify. It is NOT an aid-proof: the Markov trace on H_n(q) is a trace on a Hecke algebra, not a positive-definite function on the group S_q, so Definition 1.3's hypotheses are not known to hold in the q != 1 setting the block cares about — verifying (or refuting) them is the work, and this paper does not do it.

keyResults.statement: Defining F^n_{c,delta} as normalized positive-definite psi on S_q with |psi(rho)| <= c_l q^{-l/2} for |rho| = l and |psi(rho sigma) - psi(rho)psi(sigma)| <= delta q^{-l/2} on disjoint supports, every psi in F^n_{c,delta} is (delta + q^{-1})^{1/2}-supported on Young diagrams with |m_l(lambda) - m_l(psi)| <= K(delta + q^{-1})^{1/4} q^{l/2} for l <= n/2.
keyResults.useForFolio: Gives the explicit hypothesis list a q-analogue would need, turning clause (3) of prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton from a bare 'converges weakly' conjecture into a checkable programme: exhibit the q-Plancherel weight tilde-w_lambda as arising from a psi satisfying a q-deformed (1)+(2), then the concentration is automatic.

keyResults.statement: Under the same hypotheses, |chi^lambda(rho) - psi(rho)| <= K(delta + q^{-1})^{1/4} q^{-l/2} for all rho with |rho| = l <= n/2 — concentration stated directly on normalized character values.
keyResults.useForFolio: Character-level concentration is the form clause (2) of prop:q-plancherel-asymptotic-skeleton uses ('character fluctuations have variance O(1/sqrt(n-3))'); Thm 2 is the q=1 statement of that shape from a source that actually proves a fluctuation bound, unlike the currently-cited feray2010 (see the 0304010v1 row).

keyResults.statement: The same concentration holds for the free cumulants R_l of the transition measure: |R_l(lambda) - R_l(psi)| <= K(delta + q^{-1})^{1/4} q^{l/2}.
keyResults.useForFolio: rem:non-commutative-probability-dictionary already frames the Hecke GNS data as a non-commutative probability space with free-cumulant language; Cor. 1 is the concentration statement in exactly those coordinates, so it can be cited there without translation.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan: references.ts has biane1998 only; this is a different Biane paper and has no entry.
Clauses (1)/(2) of the block cite vershik-kerov1977 + biane1998 + feray2010; the concentration result they actually lean on is this paper's Thm 1/Thm 2.

Record what a q-deformed Definition 1.3 would have to assert, and the obstruction that the Markov trace on H_n(q) is not a positive-definite function on S_q — this turns the open clause (3) into a stated programme rather than a bare conjecture.
